sections.overview: This secretive North American forest cuckoo is a close genus-mate of the Mangrove Cuckoo, C. minor, which is more coastal.
sections.identification: A slender brown body, black bill, red eye-ring and white tail tips help identify it.
sections.habitat: It breeds in wooded edges and thickets across southern Canada and the eastern United States.
sections.diet: Caterpillars are important prey, and abundance can track outbreaks of tent caterpillars.
sections.behavior: It usually builds and tends its own nest, though it sometimes lays eggs in other birds’ nests.
sections.reproduction: The young develop quickly; Cornell reports about 17 days from egg-laying to fledging.
sections.ecology: Its abundance can respond to seasonal pulses in insect prey, especially tent caterpillars.
sections.conservation: Canadian monitoring indicates a moderate long-term decline, although annual survey results fluctuate widely.
